title: Indigenous Interiors as Narrative Spaces: Heritage Interiors as Storytellers of Memory in Hoi An Ancient Houses, Vietnam
content: Heritage interiors do not exist as historical artefacts but also serve as the narrative spaces where personal and communal memories can be stored over time, embodied, and conveyed by means of materials, furnishing, colour, light, and spatial configuration. The paper discusses indigenous interiors of ancient houses in Hoi An, a UNESCO world heritage port city located in central Vietnam and the goal of the paper is to explore interior space as a memory, identity, and urban memory teller. The paper utilises theoretical approaches to the issues of indigenous heritage, place memory and phenomenological experience to frame heritage interiors as dynamic socio-cultural processes as opposed to its material relics. The study follows a qualitative methodological approach that includes: (1) field survey of documenting architectural layouts, material conditions, and interior arrangements; (2) on-site phenomenological observations that record the sensory and experiential attributes of light, smell, sound, and spatial feel to interview experiences and memory discourses regarding interior features. Data were gathered at three ancient houses of Hoi An during the period between March and August 2024. This qualitative methodology is combined with the help of a mixed approach that will allow the research to detect both tactile and intangible strata integrated in the everyday domestic space. The results reveal that the factors like the ancestral altars, polished wood columns, carved furniture, and control of natural light by the means of inner courtyards are actively used as mnemonic devices. These aspects are collectively what this paper conceptualises as an interior memoryscape a multi-layered narrative system, where family histories, community identities, and urban heritage collide.
